questions.q: Fill: 'The meeting is ___ Monday ___ 3 o'clock ___ July.'
questions.a: on Monday, at 3 o'clock, in July — the calendar rule end to end. Wrong answers mixing the three show the rule isn't internalized as a set.

questions.q: 'She travels ___ bus daily.' in or on — and why?
questions.a: 'on' — public transport takes 'on' (on the bus/train/plane); 'in' is for cars and taxis. A wrong answer 'in' reveals Hindi-inside translation instead of the English convention.

questions.q: Between or among: 'The secret is ___ you and me' / 'She stood ___ the crowd.'
questions.a: between you and me (two), among the crowd (many). A wrong answer swapping them shows the two-vs-many split isn't yet clear.

questions.q: ______ are position words — they place things in space (in, on, under, behind, between), in time (at, on, in, since, for), and in direction (to, into, towards).

Fill in the blank: ______ are position words — they place things in space (in, on, under, behind, between), in time (at, on, in, since, for), and in direction (to, into, towards). 'The cat is ON the mat' — change the preposition and the whole picture changes.
Fill in the blank: The ______ rule is the anchor: at = exact point (at 5 o'clock), on = day/date (on Monday, on 15 August), in = longer stretches (in July, in 2024, in the morning).
What is Prepositions? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Prepositions are position words — they place things in space (in, on, under, behind, between), in time (at, on, in, since, for), and in direction (to, into, towards). 'The cat is ON the mat' — change the preposition and the whole picture changes.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Prepositions?
questions.a: Students translate from Hindi — 'in the bus' feels like 'inside' so they write 'in the bus' where English says 'on the bus' (public transport takes 'on').

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student uses space prepositions correctly (in/on/under/between/among/behind), time prepositions by the calendar rule (at+clock, on+day/date, in+month/year), and between-vs-among.
